title: Configured global time step
overview: global_dt is read by solver control initialization and loaded into Ctrl::pdt. The global time-step strategy uses this configured value; the local/global hybrid strategy later replaces pdt with the minimum computed local step.
principle: For the global strategy, the cell time-step field is filled from pdt initialized by global_dt. This is an input time increment in the active case/solver convention; its dimensional or nondimensional unit is not established universally by the audited source.
architecture: Ctrl::Init and the NS, incompressible NS, and turbulence control initializers load global_dt. UTimeStep::CalcGlobalTimeStep applies ctrl.pdt; UTimeStep::CalcLgTimeStep computes local values, takes the minimum, and stores it back into ctrl.pdt. This input is independent of the CFL ramp. MG::Run advances ctrl.currTime by ctrl.pdt: startStrategy 2 or 3 does so before each inner solve while incrementing both counters; the other branch does so once before its inner loop. This is a run-loop accumulator update, not a proof that every solver uses the same timing cadence. Ctrl::Init seeds ctrl.pdt1 from the configured initial ctrl.pdt so the first previous-step denominator is nonzero when global_dt is valid. TimeIntegration::CalcSrcCoeff and the dual-time implicit spectrum consume pdt1. No subsequent history-shift assignment was found; this seed does not establish variable-step correctness.

proves: Four solver-control initializers read global_dt into Ctrl::pdt.
The global strategy applies pdt as a common cell time step.
The local/global hybrid branch replaces pdt with the minimum local time step.
In MG::Run, currTime is incremented by pdt at the start-strategy-specific update site.
Ctrl::Init seeds pdt1 from pdt at startup.
does_not_prove: A universal unit or nondimensional scale for global_dt.
That global_dt is derived from cflst/cfled/ncfl.
That the configured value is used unchanged by the hybrid strategy.
That the chosen value guarantees stability or accuracy.
That pdt1 is advanced to the accepted previous physical time step after pdt changes, particularly in local/global hybrid stepping.

verification.scope: Source-backed input and strategy behavior; no numerical run is claimed. The MG::Run time-accumulator update is source-audited only; no physical-time integration run is claimed. Startup previous-step seeding is source-backed; variable-step history advancement and numerical dual-time integration remain unverified.

examples.title: Global versus hybrid strategy
examples.calculation: With mode 1, Ctrl::pdt starts from 0.001 and is applied as the common step. With mode 2, local steps are computed and their minimum replaces Ctrl::pdt.
examples.result: global_dt is the configured seed for global stepping, not the final hybrid step in general.
examples.limitations: The example does not establish units, nondimensional scale, or a stable step for a particular mesh and flow.

formulas.title: Global time-step state
formulas.plain: pdt = global_dt at initialization; hybrid mode updates pdt = min_c(Delta t_c)
formulas.assumptions: The first relation is the configured input initialization. The second is the audited local/global hybrid reduction; they are not simultaneously immutable.

formulas.title: Run-loop time accumulator update
formulas.plain: currTime_new = currTime_old + pdt at each MG::Run update site
formulas.assumptions: This relation describes each explicit currTime increment in MG::Run. startStrategy 2 or 3 increments before each inner solve; the other branch increments once before the inner loop.

formulas.title: Previous-step interval bootstrap
formulas.plain: pdt1 = pdt = global_dt at Ctrl initialization
formulas.assumptions: This is the startup seed only. It is not a variable-step history update rule.

symbols.meaning: Previous-step interval used by history-dependent unsteady terms

caveats: Units and nondimensional scaling depend on the active case/solver convention.
Do not conflate global_dt with the CFL ramp or the final hybrid pdt.
pdt1 is seeded from pdt at Ctrl initialization, but no subsequent history-shift assignment was found. Variable-step dual-time use is therefore not established.
